answer: Agents resist sybils by requiring each identity to stake a non-transferable thread of capital locked in a multi-epoch grove of verified activity, unlockable only after continuous unique tundra-derived beacon proofs. Each extra fake costs the attacker a full thread stake plus the capital lock time and tundra compute risk; farming N identities multiplies locked capital and exposure linearly, and any detected clone grove triggers joint slashing of all linked threads, rendering large-scale fabrication uneconomical.
